description: Slack incoming webhook integration. No existing Slack code — everything is new. The Asana integration (OAuth flow) is the structural pattern, but Slack uses a simpler webhook URL approach: no OAuth, just store a webhook URL in a DB table. The IntegrationsClient.tsx already has an IntegrationCard component that accepts onConnect/onDisconnect; we add Slack state and a connect modal to that client component.
steps: 1. Create DB migration supabase/migrations/20261023000017_slack_connections.sql: CREATE TABLE slack_connections (id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), webhook_url text NOT NULL, channel_name text NOT NULL, created_by uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()); — one row per org, enforce single row via a unique constraint on a constant expression or just rely on application logic (upsert by webhook_url uniqueness is not right; use a singleton approach: check for any existing row on connect). Enable RLS, grant service_role. Add set_updated_at trigger.

2. Add SlackConnection type to src/types/database.ts: add slack_connections table definition to Database.public.Tables (Row, Insert, Update); export type SlackConnection = Database['public']['Tables']['slack_connections']['Row']; at the bottom.

3. Create src/lib/slack.ts: export async function postSlackMessage(text: string, blocks?: object[]). Reads webhook URL from DB first (SELECT webhook_url FROM slack_connections LIMIT 1); falls back to process.env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL if no DB row. If neither exists, returns early (graceful no-op). Posts via fetch to the webhook URL with { text, blocks } body. Catches and logs errors without throwing.
4. Add SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL= (empty) to .env.local under a new # ─── Slack section comment above the # Cron section.

5. Create src/app/api/integrations/slack/connect/route.ts: POST handler. Auth: getServerSession + can(role, 'manage_system'). Body: { webhook_url: string, channel_name: string }. Validate: webhook_url must start with https://hooks.slack.com/. Delete existing slack_connections row (if any), then insert new row with { webhook_url, channel_name, created_by: session.user.id }. Returns { ok: true }.
6. Create src/app/api/integrations/slack/disconnect/route.ts: DELETE handler. Auth: getServerSession + can(role, 'manage_system'). Deletes all rows from slack_connections. Returns { ok: true }.

7. Create src/app/api/integrations/slack/status/route.ts: GET handler. Auth: getServerSession. Queries SELECT channel_name FROM slack_connections LIMIT 1. Returns { connected: boolean, channel_name: string | null }.

8. Update src/features/settings/components/IntegrationsClient.tsx: (a) Add SlackConnection interface and slackStatus prop to Props. (b) Add slack state (connected boolean, channelName string). (c) Add connectSlack async function that opens a new modal state (showSlackModal boolean). (d) Add disconnectSlack async function that calls DELETE /api/integrations/slack/disconnect. (e) Move the Slack card out of the 'Coming soon' grid into a new SettingsSection titled 'Messaging' with description 'Connect messaging tools for automated notifications'. (f) Render IntegrationCard for Slack with status derived from slackStatus.connected, onConnect opens modal, onDisconnect calls disconnectSlack. (g) Add a simple inline modal (using SimpleModal) for webhook URL and channel name inputs; on submit POST /api/integrations/slack/connect, update state on success. Keep Google Calendar, BambooHR, Workday in Coming soon.

9. Update src/app/(app)/settings/integrations/page.tsx: query slack_connections table (SELECT channel_name, 1 row). Pass slackStatus={{ connected: Boolean(slackRow), channelName: slackRow?.channel_name ?? null }} to IntegrationsClient.
acceptance_criteria: src/lib/slack.ts exports postSlackMessage that is a no-op when no webhook is configured
POST /api/integrations/slack/connect returns 200 for admin/hr, 403 for other roles
Slack card appears as a real integration (not in Coming soon) in IntegrationsClient
verification: npm run build — must exit 0 with no TypeScript errors
npm run lint — no new errors in changed files
